title: Skybase's governance-frontend obligation is an availability and continuity commitment, not just a hosting arrangement
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3.2.3 states Skybase's strategy for the Core Governance Reward Primitive as providing "continuous, secure, and user-friendly governance frontend hosting for SKY holders, ensuring critical decision-making processes remain accessible and reliable over time."

Two guiding criteria give it teeth. Security & Reliability: "The Prime Agent will uphold robust security measures and maintain high availability to prevent disruptions or unauthorized access." And Governance Framework Alignment: "Any updates to the frontend should integrate smoothly with Skybase's existing governance mechanisms, preserving uninterrupted voting and proposal workflows."

The second criterion is the more unusual one. It constrains Skybase's own product development: a frontend change that breaks a voting flow is a governance failure, not a release bug. An Agent whose stated mission is user-friendly interface innovation is thereby held to a stability obligation on the one surface where iteration is most dangerous.

The stakes come from the Artifact's own dependencies. The Root Edit process for Skybase itself runs through Snapshot polls and Sky Forum posts, and the ecosystem's voting portal is vote.sky.money — a Sky.money subdomain that Skybase operates (A.6.1.1.4.1). An availability failure at Skybase is therefore an availability failure of Sky governance, including the mechanism by which Skybase could be corrected.

What the provision lacks is a measurable standard. "High availability" carries no target, no monitoring requirement and no consequence for breach, so enforcement rests on the same Facilitator alignment judgment that governs everything else rather than on a service-level test.
description: The Core Governance Reward Strategy commits the Agent to robust security, high availability and to preserving uninterrupted voting and proposal workflows across frontend updates.
